title: LGD formula evaluates to zero, nulling every capital requirement
content:
**Side A — the normative text.** A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.2 specifies `LGD = min(1 - recovery, 0)`. Since `recovery` is a rate in [0,1], `1 - recovery` is non-negative, so the `min` with 0 always yields **0 or less**. Any capital requirement multiplied by LGD therefore collapses to zero.

**Side B — the reference implementation.** The Atlas embeds working code for the same model that uses `max(0, min(..., 1))` — the standard clamp, which is what the prose evidently intends.

The two cannot both be right. Read literally, the specification nulls the entire Financial Risk Capital charge; read as the code does, it behaves sensibly. This matters beyond a typo because the Atlas is the normative artifact — an implementer following the text rather than the sample would produce a system that requires no capital at all.

**To resolve:** confirm with Sky whether deployed implementations follow the code, and whether the prose is scheduled for correction.
description: A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.2 defines LGD = min(1 - recovery, 0), which is always <= 0. The Atlas's own reference implementation uses max(0, min(...,1)), confirming the bound is reversed.
